Q: Anaconda install error - conda-script.py [-h] [-V] command A:

If you type: conda -V

you can tell whether conda is installed or not. If it is installed try typing: conda update conda. if that works try running Pyton and see what you get. If the above commands fail, i would restart your computer and run the Anaconda uninstaller. You should have access to this from the Anacondapage. Now try to reinstall Anaconda.

Q: Github-Jenkins Integration > Error received as 'Last Delivery was not successful. Couldn't connect to server' A:

Look at this answer: IP address of localhost:8080 -in webhooks of github +jenkins

"You need a public address for Github to point to when detected a push request. localhost is on your localmachine."

That answer explains how to setup ngrok which will give you a public IP and will allow you to setup your webhook.

Q: Could not connect to http-remoting - Maven-Wildfly plugin A:

The reason of the problem could be one of the following:

  • The deployment of any archive (jar, war, ear) through wildfly-maven-plugin plugin will happen only if the WildFly is listening at its management port which is 9990 by default. So make sure that WildFly is listening at its management port.
  • If WildFly is listening at its management port then check if your host file located at %SYSTEM_ROOT%\System32\drivers\etc for windows machine is configured correctly. i.e. your local host is mapped correctly for both IPv4 and IPv6.

127.0.0.1 localhost

::1 localhost

Q: Loading data from MySQL and populating dropdown select with jQuery Mobile, PHP A:

I think it has todo with timing between DOM ready and executing the Jquery script.

In this case your script executes before the DOM is ready. If some objects you are refering to, arent ready yet in the DOM, thus JQuery cant find the object, then JQuery simply stops executing.

Q: How to write a CodeIgniter query builder script with AND and OR logic in the WHERE clause A:

simply: $this->db->where("status","live")->or_where("status","dead");

                               or
    $this->db->where("(status='live' OR status='dead')");

Q: How to create a list of factories with one value incremented A:

Very late to the game, but the simplest factorybot answer is to use build_list to build the records without saving them, and then the block logic to update the field that needs to increment before saving:

    build_list(:my_factory, 10) do |record, idx|
      record.unique_field = idx + 1
      record.save!
    end
